title: Fewshot attenuation heuristics — lab notes
body:
Purpose
Quick personal scratchpad capturing experiments and heuristics for reducing exemplar overdominance in few-shot prompt sets (what I call 'attenuation') — aim: keep exemplar signal useful but avoid literal copying, brittle token-level overfit, and instruction hijacking.

Background / rationale
- Problem: when small numbers of exemplars are highly similar or strongly formatted, model tends to: copy exact phrasing, overfit label tokens, or treat examples as hard rules instead of cues. This shows up as hallucinated metadata, hallucinated reasoning steps, or brittle failures on paraphrase inputs.
- Goal: heuristics that are cheap to test in hosted/Dedicated flows; prefer prompt-side fixes (no fine-tuning) that interact well with Redwood runtime features: prefix caching, batching, and token-budget SLOs.

Experiment log (chronological)
1) baseline 3-shot (A)
- Template: \"Instructions: Paraphrase to plain English. Example 1 -> Q: \"What is the meaning of life?\" A: \"Life means...\"\" (simple exact format)
- Observed: 36% verbatim reuse for unique phrases, 18% hallucinated numeric claims.

2) example-noise (B) — tiny perturbations
- Apply light paraphrase to exemplars (tense swap, synonym replace). Keep labels same.
- Observed: small reduction in verbatim copying (~22%) but occasional polarity flips (because paraphrase introduced negation in two examples).

3) anchor-token dilution (C)
- Insert neutral anchor sentence before each example: \"(Example for style only; ignore facts.)\"
- Observed: Large drop in factual hallucination (13%), but model ignored label formatting more frequently -> answer brevity decreased.

4) exemplar-weighting via explicit meta cues (D)
- Prefix: \"Examples are guides, not rules. Provide your own phrasing.\" and add \"EXAMPLE_START\" tokens between examples (unique sequence).
- Observed: Better paraphrase diversity; lower exact-match. Slight latency + token usage increase (anchor tokens counted).

5) negative-exemplar (E)
- Include 1 negative example showing what *not* to do.
- Observed: helped on structure errors but introduced confusion when negative example had contradictory label tokens.

Quick takeaway: combination of paraphrase augmentation + explicit \"guidance\" prefix seems promising. Anchors reduce hallucination but cost tokens.

Prototype heuristics (to test systematically)
- ShotRotation: rotate order of exemplars per request to avoid position bias (cheap, interacts badly with caching — needs route-aware cache bypass).
- SoftParaphrasePool: maintain pool of 5 paraphrase variants per exemplar; sample 1–2 per prompt. Reduces verbatim reuse.
- AnchorLite: single short anchor token phrase (\"Style guide: be original.\") vs full sentence; measure delta/loss ratio.
- ExampleContrast: for categorical tasks, include 1 borderline example to widen model boundary; for generative tasks include 1 counterexample to show failure modes.
- TokenBudget-aware truncation: if request close to budget, automatically switch to AnchorLite + 1-shot.

Failure modes observed / notes
- Instruction hijacking: too many meta-cues cause model to treat prompt like a multi-step instruction list and follow the wrong step. Keep meta-language short.
- Contradictory anchors: negative examples that contradict label vocabulary can flip final labels. Use neutral phrasing for negatives (show format, not content).
- Caching/cold-start interaction: rotating exemplars defeats prefix caching; for high-QPS routes, prefer static exemplar unless you have hot cache invalidation.

Sample prompt prototypes (short)
1) SoftParaphrase 3-shot (compact)
\"GUIDE: Use your own words. \nExample 1:\nQ: How to reset my router?\nA: Turn it off, wait 30s, turn on.\n--\nExample 2:\nQ: Steps to cancel subscription?\nA: Sign in, go to billing, click cancel.\n--\nNow answer:\nQ: {{user_q}}\n\"

2) AnchorLite + negative (compact)
\"Style: concise, do not echo examples exactly.\nBAD EXAMPLE:\nQ: What is pi?\nA: 3.14159 EXACT (do not mirror)\nGOOD EXAMPLES:\n... (2 positive paraphrased examples)\nAnswer: {{user_q}}\n\"

Measurement plan (automated)
- Metrics: exact-token overlap rate, n-gram reuse, paraphrase-similarity (embedding cosine to exemplars), faithfulness score (task-specific), token cost delta, 95th pct latency.
- Dataset: 400 eval queries per template; include paraphrase + adversarial variants.
- Compare across: baseline static-3shot, SoftParaphrase, AnchorLite, Rotation-once-per-1000, Negative-example. Use Redwood Dedicated for consistent latency measurement.

Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: How much does exemplar diversity interact with model size/quantization? run small-medium-large (ggml/FP16/8-bit) matrix.
- Q2: Should we expose attenuation knobs in the SDK (e.g., sample_paraphrase_count, anchor_level)? sketch API surface.
- Q3: Best practice doc: one-pager for Solutions team summarizing heuristics + when to prefer server-side cache bypass. Draft outline needed.

Action items (short)
- [ ] Run 5k evaluation across two models and log metrics (owner: Jonas) — Linear-4821
- [ ] Prototype SDK flags for AnchorLite and ShotRotation (owner: me) — drop-in param: attenuation: {none, lite, full}
- [ ] Short internal note for Solutions with examples and recommended defaults (owner: Priya)

Rough notes to self (messy)
- prefer 1–2 short anchors instead of long meta paragraphs; long ones break model flow
- negative exemplars should not reuse label tokens; use neutral markers like \"LABEL:X\" to show format only
- consider embedding-cluster sampling to pick exemplars that are diverse w.r.t. user query (but cost is extra lookup)
- remember: batching + shared prompt templates can accidentally leak anchoring if not per-request randomized

Snippets / quick experiments to copy into test harness
- bash pseudo: \nfor MODEL in rwd-xl rwd-medium; do run_eval --template softparaphrase --paraphrases 3 --samples 1; done

References / links for myself
- internal: RFC: fewshot-guidance-patterns (confluence id: 8743)
- external: paper on instruction induction: \"When Prompts Collude\" (noted in reading list)

End of pad.

(Notes intentionally rough — keep evolving. Will move to a more polished playbook if evaluation results look promising.)
